body:
If you are researching full-arch tooth replacement, you have probably seen the term All-on-X. This guide explains what it means, how treatment unfolds step by step, what it typically costs, and the caveats that rarely appear in advertising. For how we plan these cases in our Valencia office, start with our [All-on-4 implants](/services/oral-surgery/all-on-4-implants/) overview.

## What All-on-X means

All-on-X is a family of full-arch implant treatments. An entire upper or lower set of teeth is replaced with a fixed bridge supported by a small number of implants. The X is the number of implants, commonly four (All-on-4), sometimes six or more. Because the bridge is attached to the implants rather than resting on the gums, it restores chewing, speech and facial support in a way a removable denture cannot.

## Why the variations exist

Dr. Neda Moezzi chooses between All-on-4, All-on-6, zygomatic implants or a hybrid approach based on bone anatomy, medical history and prosthetic goals. Two differences matter most:

- **Implant count and spread.** More implants can improve long-term biomechanics, at the cost of more surgery and higher fees.
- **Immediate versus staged teeth.** Many protocols attach a provisional fixed bridge the same day as surgery. The definitive prosthesis is delivered after the implants integrate, usually several months later.

## How treatment works

### Step 1: assessment and 3D planning

Planning starts with a clinical exam, photographs and a cone beam CT (CBCT) scan. Digital planning software maps implant positions that will support a fixed arch while avoiding nerves and sinuses, and guided surgery carries that plan into the operating room. This reduces surprises on the day. For imaging and timing details, see [how long dental implants take](/how-long-do-dental-implants-take/).

### Step 2: extractions and bone work, if needed

Most All-on-X patients still have some teeth that need to come out. Where bone volume is short, grafting or alternative anchorage is considered. The aim is a stable platform for the implants.

### Step 3: implant placement and provisional teeth

The implants are placed according to the plan. Often a provisional fixed bridge is attached the same day, so you leave with anchored teeth. The provisional protects the surgical site and lets you function while the implants heal.

### Step 4: integration and the final prosthesis

After three to six months of healing, the provisional is replaced with a definitive prosthesis built for long-term wear. The final restoration is stronger and more lifelike than the provisional.

## All-on-X compared with other options

These are typical U.S. ranges, not our fees. Your written estimate will differ.

| Metric | All-on-X (fixed full arch) | Individual implants (tooth by tooth) | Traditional dentures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Typical U.S. price | $15,000 to $50,000 per arch, depending on materials and lab | $3,000 to $6,000 per tooth (fixture plus crown) | $600 to $8,000 for a complete set |
| Immediate function | Often yes (provisional the same day) | Sometimes, in select cases | Yes, removable |
| Bone preservation | Yes, implants transfer load to bone | Yes | No |
| Maintenance | Daily hygiene and routine professional care; risk of peri-implant disease | Daily care; individual crowns may need periodic service | Daily removal and cleaning; relines over time |

## What the evidence shows

Across studies, long-term implant survival often falls between 90 and 98 percent at ten years, depending on patient factors and prosthesis type. A systematic review in the [National Library of Medicine](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4647895/) summarizes the data. Keep in mind that fixture survival is one measure; prosthetic wear, maintenance and satisfaction are separate questions.

## What drives the cost

All-on-X uses fewer implants than replacing every tooth individually, which is why it can be the more efficient route to a full arch. The final figure still depends on:

- The number of implants and whether grafting or a sinus lift is needed.
- The final prosthesis material: acrylic on titanium, hybrid zirconia or layered ceramic.
- Surgeon and lab expertise, and local market factors.

For local pricing context and an itemized checklist to bring to a consultation, read our [dental implants Valencia cost guide](/dental-implants-valencia-cost-guide/).

## What patients say

Online patient discussions are not scientific samples, but they repeat three themes: surprise bills when estimates were not itemized, infections and delays in patients with poorly controlled diabetes, and wide variation in what offices include in a quote. The lessons are practical. Get the estimate in writing, treat your general health as part of the plan, and seek a second opinion for complex full-arch cases.

## Who is a good candidate

Good candidates have controlled medical conditions, adequate bone or a willingness to graft, and realistic expectations about maintenance. Higher risk or contraindications include uncontrolled diabetes, heavy smoking, active untreated gum disease, and recent head or neck radiation. When risks exist, we discuss alternatives such as implant-retained overdentures or staged treatment.

## Complications and long-term care

The most common issues after All-on-X are prosthetic wear, loose screws, and peri-implant mucositis or peri-implantitis (inflammation and bone loss around implants). Catching these early takes regular professional checkups and careful home care. Smoking and diabetes raise the risk of complications and should be managed before surgery.

## Questions to ask at your consultation

- Which All-on-X variant do you recommend for my anatomy, and why?
- Can you show before-and-after cases similar to mine?
- Do you use CBCT-based guided surgery, and is it included in the estimate?
- What are the itemized costs for surgery, implants, the provisional, the definitive prosthesis, lab fees and follow-up?
- How will my medical conditions or medications affect candidacy?

## When to get a second opinion

If a quoted plan has no CBCT assessment, the clinic cannot provide an itemized estimate, or your medical history raises concerns, get a second opinion before irreversible steps such as extractions and implant surgery.

## All-on-X versus an implant-retained overdenture

| Feature | All-on-X (fixed) | Implant-retained overdenture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stability and chewing | High; the bridge is fixed | Good; removable but snaps onto implants |
| Cost | Higher upfront, though fewer implants than tooth by tooth | Lower than a fixed arch; often 2 to 4 implants |
| Maintenance | Professional cleanings, occasional prosthetic repairs | Daily removal for cleaning, periodic relines |

## Next steps

All-on-X can give many patients a fixed, functional arch, but candidacy, cost and long-term care vary from person to person. Bring your questions, expect a CBCT scan and a written itemized estimate, and consider a second opinion if anything is unclear. For more context, compare [dental implants vs dentures](/dental-implants-vs-dentures/), then call (661) 254-5200 to schedule imaging and a treatment review with Dr. Moezzi.

faq.q: What is the recovery like after All-on-X surgery?
faq.a: Expect a few days of swelling and moderate discomfort controlled with prescribed medication. Many patients manage soft foods within a week while wearing the immediate provisional. Full bone integration takes three to six months, depending on health and whether grafting was needed.

faq.q: How long does an All-on-X prosthesis last?
faq.a: Implant fixtures can last decades with proper care. The prosthetic teeth and acrylic base typically need maintenance or replacement over a 10 to 15 year span, depending on wear. Regular checkups catch mechanical or biological problems early.

Typical U.S. ranges run from about $15,000 to $50,000 per arch, depending on implant count, prosthesis materials, lab fees and any grafting. Ask for a written breakdown. Our dental implants Valencia cost guide includes an itemized checklist to bring to a consultation.

faq.q: Can I get All-on-X if I have worn dentures for years?
faq.a: Often yes. Long-term denture wear can cause bone loss, but angled implants, zygomatic anchorage or grafting can make a fixed solution possible. A CBCT scan is essential to determine feasibility.

faq.q: Is All-on-X painful compared with dentures?
faq.a: Surgery involves a healing period, but many patients report better long-term comfort and function with fixed implant-supported teeth than with unstable dentures. Post-operative discomfort is managed with medication and usually eases within days to weeks.

Coverage varies widely. Many plans cover diagnostics and part of the prosthetic work but treat implants as elective. Get pre-authorization and a written benefits estimate before surgery so you can plan financing if needed.
